label: Susan Gough
narrative: Gough was, for roughly six years, the single voice through which the Department of Defense spoke on UAP, and the record of what she said is unusually complete because Elizondo wrote to her directly and those emails were released under FOIA 21-F-0938. On 13 June 2019 she told The Black Vault that Harry Reid's newly authenticated 2009 SAP-request memorandum 'makes no change to previous statements. Mr. Elizondo had no assigned responsibilities for AATIP while he was in OUSD(I).' On 6 December 2019 she went further and repudiated her own colleague, stating 'Neither AATIP nor AAWSAP were UAP related' and that 'when implemented, AATIP did not pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena' — explaining that Christopher Sherwood had merely been 'repeating the information that had been provided by a previous spokesperson some two years earlier' and that the earlier spokesperson 'is no longer with my organization.' On 21 May 2021 she partially reversed again, conceding that the AATIP contract 'allowed for research drawn from a wide variety of sources, including reports of UAPs' while insisting 'the examination of UAP observations was not the purpose of AATIP.' Elizondo wrote to her on 3 June 2020: 'You released a statement claiming I had no assigned duties in the AATIP program. The truth, as everyone involved in the program knows, is that I ran the program.' In his November 2024 written testimony he told Congress that the Pentagon's use of 'a professional psychological operations officer' as its primary UAP contact was 'unacceptable' — a reference to Gough's career field.
